**Going out:** Email to Tom, subject "A new green tea", announcing a Japanese sencha.

**Claims check:** The copy makes no statistics, superlatives, guarantees, testimonials, or urgency claims. "Grassy and a little sweet" and the 70 degree brewing guidance are product facts, which the policy says the product team has checked and are fine as written. "We've added a Japanese sencha to the shop" is a new-product statement, also covered as a product fact.

**Regulated claims:** No health, money, legal, environmental, children or price content.

**House style:** Voice is warm, plain and unhurried. No banned words and no AI tells. Score about 92. Nothing to change.

**Disclosure:** This is the brand's own email about its own product. No paid partnership, affiliate link, gift or AI-labelling trigger applies.

**Fixed:** Nothing needed changing.

**Needs a decision:** Nothing unresolved.

**Approver:** Sam (marketing lead). The email is clean, but it can't go out until Sam gives an explicit yes to this exact content. I haven't recorded any approval, and I won't do so on Sam's behalf. Once Sam approves, the email can be sent.
